Subject: Hosted API — queued requests/backlog observed in us-west (status update)

Hi Alan / GreenLeaf SRE team,

Quick note to let you know we are investigating an elevated queue length and growing request backlog affecting hosted inference endpoints in the us-west region (text-generation endpoints and some chat routes). Symptoms we see:
- P50 latency elevated from ~60ms to ~220ms and P95 spiking above 1.2s for affected routes
- Queued requests visible in the router with retry/timeout churn for a subset of customers
- Autoscaler reported errors for one GPU pool (pool-id: gpool-17) starting ~08:52 PDT

We have opened an incident (RLC-2026-08-20) and published an initial status page entry: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/RLC-2026-08-20.

Immediate actions: Marcus and Laura are investigating root cause; we have temporarily diverted new traffic to other pools where capacity is available. I'm cc'ing our SRE/CS leads so we can keep you updated in this thread.

Attachments: incident-dashboard.png (screenshot of queue growth), request-log-snippet.txt (sample request traces).

Please reply here if you're seeing increased errors or timeouts on your side — any logs/examples help. We will post another update within 30 minutes or when we have a mitigation confirmed.

—Stephanie

Subject: Re: Hosted API — queued requests/backlog observed in us-west (status update)

Stephanie / Marcus,

Quick internal summary of findings so far (internal recipients only):
- Root suspected: recent NVIDIA driver rollout to a subset of hosts in gpool-17 resulted in intermittent GPU device hangs and a high rate of kernel timeouts on 3/12 hosts. The autoscaler interpreted host flakiness as instance churn and failed to stabilize pod counts.
- Impacted surface: text-generation model variants that require full KV cache (large-context routes) were the most affected — smaller models continued to serve from other pools.
- Mitigation applied at 09:08 PDT: rolled back the driver on the 3 affected hosts and forced a drain/restart sequence. Manually scaled gpool-17 + spun up two warm instances from warm-pool to absorb peak.
- Observed: queue length began to drop at ~09:20 PDT; backend error rate now trending down.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Keep gpool-17 isolated from automatic driver rollouts until we validate a fix.
2) Run a targeted soak of the rollback hosts under synthetic traffic for 1 hour.
3) Prepare an RCA draft and coordinate messaging for a public postmortem.

I'll add the debug snippets to the incident board (INF-4921).

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Hosted API — queued requests/backlog observed in us-west (status update)

Alan — quick update for GreenLeaf:

Thank you for the logs you sent (we pulled the traces). We confirmed the backlog was caused by a driver rollout that produced intermittent GPU hangs on a small subset of hosts in the gpool-17 capacity pool. Our actions:
- Rolled back the driver on affected hosts and drained/restarted pods (09:08–09:18 PDT)
- Manually scaled additional capacity from warm pool to absorb the backlog (09:10–09:25 PDT)
- Enabled automatic fallback to a compatible model variant for requests that would otherwise queue (applied 09:22 PDT)

Current status: backlog cleared across affected routes; P95 latencies have returned to normal for most traffic. We will keep the rollback in place while we validate the driver patch.

We will prepare a short post-incident summary and a full RCA within 72 hours. I will also add a note on the status page once the RCA is published. If you experienced any lingering errors or timeouts after 09:30 PDT, please let me know and include any sample request IDs.

Attachment: incident-dashboard.png (current snapshot).

—Stephanie

Subject: [Postmortem] RLC-2026-08-20 — queued requests in us-west (summary & next steps)

Hi Alan and GreenLeaf team —

We wanted to follow up with a concise post-incident summary and next steps. A longer RCA is attached in draft form and will be published to the status page once finalized.

Incident summary (impact window):
- Start: 2026-08-20 08:52 PDT — Autoscaler errors and queue growth observed in gpool-17
- Mitigation complete: 2026-08-20 09:30 PDT — Driver rollback + manual scale absorbed backlog; fallbacks enabled
- Total customer-visible impact window: ~38 minutes

Root cause: A targeted driver rollout introduced instability on 3 hosts in gpool-17, causing GPU device timeouts. The autoscaler misinterpreted host issues and failed to restore capacity quickly enough to prevent queueing for large-context routes.

Corrective actions (already done):
- Rolled back GPU driver on affected hosts; added hold on further rollouts for the pool
- Manually scaled capacity and enabled fallback routing for model variants

Follow-up actions (planned):
- Engineering: Improve autoscaler heuristics to detect host-level driver-induced flakiness (INF-4921)
- Platform: Add pre-rollout device health checks and a staging soak for driver updates
- Customer comms: Publish formal RCA on status page and offer one-on-one postmortem with platform SRE if desired

Links: RCA draft (internal) https://drive.redwood.example/file/d/1a2b3c-rca-draft, Jira INF-4921: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4921, status page entry: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/RLC-2026-08-20

If you'd like us to schedule a short call to walk through the technical details and mitigation timeline, let me know your availability and we will coordinate.

Thanks again for your patience and for the quick log samples — they were helpful.

—Stephanie
